cluster_name: US forces complete Iraq withdrawal ending Operation Inherent Resolve
event_summary: On September 30, 2026, the last U.S. and coalition troops departed Erbil Air Base in Iraq, ending Operation Inherent Resolve after 12 years. The withdrawal was negotiated in 2024 under Biden and executed under Trump, with the U.S. military headquarters relocating to Jordan.
tldr: The withdrawal is physically one event, but the corpus fractures into three incompatible narratives: an orderly mission success (Pentagon/Fox News/CGTN), a strategic blunder that leaves a power vacuum (Foreign Policy/War on the Rocks/Asia Times), and an Iranian-Russian victory (IRNA/Tehran Times/RT/TASS). The most striking fault line is that the ‘blunder’ and ‘victory’ frames converge on the same underlying claim — the US failed — even as they serve entirely different audiences. Iran’s IRGC uses the moment not just to declare a ‘historic victory’ but to announce a new phase of regional assertiveness and warn that ‘the era of cost-free threats against Iran is over.’ Baghdad’s own framing — that the departure proves Iraq’s ‘increasing strength and sovereignty’ — appears only through the Canadian Globe and Mail; no Iraqi outlet is present in the corpus.

frames.sub_frame: ISIS mission concluded, power vacuum risk

evidence.quote: The United States and its allies have completed a 12-year military operation against the militant group Islamic State in Iraq, the Pentagon said on Wednesday, as US forces prepare to leave their final bases in the country by the end of the day.

Operation Inherent Resolve is scheduled to end on Sept. 30, as remaining U.S. troops in northern Iraq complete their withdrawal. The United States formed Combined Joint Task Force – Operation Inherent Resolve in October 2014 to bring together partners to combat the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL), which had seized territory in parts of Iraq and Syria. The end of Operation Inherent Resolve highlights the success of coalition efforts against ISIL but also raises questions about future
The U.S. military completed its withdrawal from Erbil Air Base, ending Operation Inherent Resolve in Iraq while relocating its headquarters to Jordan.

Tehran, IRNA – Commander of the Quds Force of the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC), Brigadier General Esmaeil Qa’ani, says the United States has been expelled from Iraq and has suffered a humiliating defeat against Iran.
Iran’s Revolutionary Guards hailed Thursday the withdrawal of U.S. forces from Iraq as a "historic victory" and called for American troops to leave the Middle East entirely.
The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has welcomed the US pullout from Iraq, saying that it should also leave other countries in the region
Washington’s adversaries, including Iran and the Islamic State, are likely to take advantage of the pullout.

outlet_isolation_top.note: Most isolated bucket; Asia Times pairs the withdrawal with ongoing US bombing of Iran, a juxtaposition absent from all other coverage.
Iranian state outlets (IRNA + Tehran Times) use adversarial defeat/expulsion vocabulary that diverges semantically from the neutral withdrawal framing dominant elsewhere.

outlet_exclusive_vocab_highlights.what_it_reveals: Iranian state media vocabulary foregrounds deterrence and institutional identity — the IRGC Quds Force framing positions this as a forward-looking strategic win, not just a retrospective departure.
Only coverage to pair withdrawal ('leaving') with active military strikes ('bombing') — flagging the contradiction in US regional posture that no other outlet names.

a.quote: President Trump, never one for understatement, described the whole enterprise as “a very expensive excursion into Hell.” For once, the hyperbole is closer to the truth

b.quote: US incursion in Iraq entailed decades of instability in entire region — Russian diplomat

paradox.joint_conclusion: A pan-Asian Western-aligned commentary outlet and Russian state media’s export arm both reach the same verdict — the Iraq venture was costly and destabilizing — despite opposite geopolitical orientations. The White House’s ‘victory’ framing has no takers outside narrowly pro-administration US coverage.

silences.what_they_covered_instead: No Iraqi outlet appears in the corpus; Baghdad’s framing of the withdrawal as evidence of national sovereignty is relayed only via the Canadian Globe and Mail.
The UK was a principal OIR coalition partner but contributes no items; British press on this date appears to have covered domestic political news rather than the withdrawal milestone.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only outlet to use ‘expelled’ — framing the withdrawal as a US military defeat rather than a planned exit, with no Western outlet contesting or acknowledging this characterisation.
Links the withdrawal to ‘a new Phase for the Resistance Front across West Asia’, signalling that Iran reads this moment as a regional strategic opening, not just a bilateral win.
Issues an explicit deterrence warning calibrated to a named precedent: any aggression will be met with a response ‘more devastating than Operation True Promise 2’.
Only outlet to relay Baghdad’s own framing that the departure signals Iraq’s ‘increasing strength and sovereignty’ — a third narrative absent from US and Iranian coverage.
Headline ‘Leaving Iraq while bombing Iran’ is the only item to flag the contradiction of simultaneous US withdrawal from Iraq and ongoing military strikes against Iran.
Leads with ‘human cost of US intervention’ framing rather than mission outcome or geopolitical victory — a legacy-accountability angle no other outlet takes.
The only Western outlet to frame the withdrawal explicitly as leaving a power vacuum, naming Iran and the Islamic State as likely beneficiaries.
Provides the most complete factual timeline including the Biden-era origin of the withdrawal agreement — neutral-factual rather than celebratory or critical.

bottom_line: Thirteen outlets across nine country-buckets converge on the same physical fact — US troops left Iraq on September 30 — but split three ways on meaning: mission accomplished, strategic blunder, or Iranian victory. The paradox is that Western commentary and Russian state media agree the venture failed; only narrowly pro-administration US coverage claims success.
